name: Lawona Jane (Briggs) Anderson
paragraphs: Lawona Jane (Briggs) Anderson, 91, peacefully passed away on October 13, 2026 in Ogden, Utah.

Lawona was born on April 16, 1935, in her family’s log cabin in Manila, Utah. She often fondly recalled how her father paid for her delivery with a large wagon full of hay. She enjoyed a happy childhood surrounded by siblings, cousins, and extended family. Growing up, she loved riding horses, sewing, crocheting, and spending time outdoors.

One of the greatest joys of Lawona’s life began when she married her eternal sweetheart, Keith Anderson. She would often say, “I was the rancher’s daughter who married the sheepherder’s son.” On August 22, 1956, they were sealed for time and all eternity in the Salt Lake Temple, beginning a beautiful love story that would last a lifetime.

Keith and Lawona shared a love that was truly extraordinary. They were not only husband and wife, but the very best of friends. Through all of life’s adventures, joys, and challenges, they remained each other’s favorite person and greatest companion. Their happiest moments were simply those spent together. Their marriage was a beautiful example of unwavering love, friendship, devotion, and commitment. Together, they created a legacy of love that will forever be cherished by their 4 children and their spouses, 15 grandchildren, and 25 great-grandchildren. Keith and Lawona remained devoted to their family, finding their greatest joy in their children, grandchildren, and growing posterity.

Throughout their life together, Keith and Lawona shared countless adventures, traveling and making memories wherever life took them. Lawona was a gifted elementary school teacher who touched the lives of many children throughout her career. Keith’s work within the FAA took their family to Seattle, Los Angeles, Hawaii, Chicago, and Utah.

Following their retirement in Huntsville, Utah, Keith and Lawona continued their life of love and service by serving a mission together for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Long Beach, California. Upon returning home, they faithfully served as temple ordinance workers in the Ogden Utah Temple. They often reflected on the joy it brought them to serve their Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

Lawona will be lovingly remembered as a devoted wife, mother, and grandmother; a cherished friend; wonderful storyteller; and talented seamstress. She enjoyed crocheting countless afghans and hot pads for those she loved. Her enthusiasm for missionary work and devotion to her faith were an important part of her life. She leaves behind a beautiful legacy of love, kindness, and faith.
Her family finds great comfort in knowing Lawona is reunited in the loving arms of her “handsome cowboy,” Keith, whom she missed so dearly for the past 15 years.
The family has asked that in lieu in flowers, donations can be made to a favorite charity of your choice in her honor.

Lawona's viewing will be held from 10:00 to 11:15 a.m. at the Huntsville 2nd Ward: 277 S. 7400 E. in Huntsville, Utah with a graveside service to follow at Huntsville Cemetery on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

We invite family and friends who all loved Lawona to please share memories and photos of her on her memorial page at https://my.gather.app/remember/lawona-anderson-2026, so we may see her beautiful life through your eyes.
